title: Filtered finite-complex-heart closure on qcqs pro-etale sites
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; in particular it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\mathcal C_X$ be the finite constant scalar-model constructible modules of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For a cochain complex $K^\bullet$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] having only finitely many nonzero terms, all in $\mathcal C_X$, set
$$N_K=H^0(K^\bullet)=\ker(d^0:K^0\to K^1)/\operatorname{im}(d^{-1}:K^{-1}\to K^0).$$
The differentials are arbitrary module-sheaf maps; $N_K$ need not be constructible. Let $\mathcal I_X$ be the replete class of modules isomorphic to small filtered colimits in $\mathcal A_X$ of the modules $N_K$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Diagram arrows may be arbitrary module maps and need not lift to chain maps. Then $\mathcal I_X$ contains zero and $\mathcal C_X$, is closed under kernels and cokernels of all morphisms between its members, under all ambient extensions, and under all small ambient coproducts. Ambient extension closure means that every exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ with $M',M''\in\mathcal I_X$ has $M\in\mathcal I_X$, without a supplied finite-stage lift. All resulting presentations use the same indexing universe. The Noetherian hypothesis is required for this heart argument. No absolute cohomological-dimension bound, affineness, characteristic restriction, invertibility of $\ell$ or completeness of the modules is assumed. Empty schemes and zero coefficient rings are included.

proof.text: On the small pro-étale site, the essentially-small-site form of the sieve-site Grothendieck theorem gives a Grothendieck abelian category of abelian sheaves. The sheaf tensor is additive, and tensoring preserves colimits. Apply Mod.isGrothendieckAbelian to the actual coefficient ring object to obtain the ambient Grothendieck module category, with colimits in universe u+1.

proof.text: The Noetherian scalar-model heart theorem applies to this $X$ and precisely these six coefficients, including all continuous $\Omega$-valued functions. It makes the full replete category $\mathcal C_X$ essentially small, containing zero, and closed under ambient kernels, cokernels and extensions. It includes the finitely presented integral torsion models, rather than only locally free modules.

proof.text: For a finite complex K, kernel closure puts Z=ker(d^0) in the constructible class. Mathlib homologyIsCokernel identifies H^0(K) directly as coker(K^(-1) -> Z), so cokernel closure puts it in the same class without a separate image object. Transport across the isomorphism in the finite-heart presentation. Conversely the single complex C[0] has finite support and constructible terms (zero away from degree zero); its homology is C. Thus finiteConstructibleComplexHearts equals the constructible class, and their small filtered-colimit hulls agree. No chain-map lifts are used.

proof.text: Use noetherian_scalar_constructible_fp2 for every small filtered ambient diagram. Its Hom comparison gives preservation by additive coyoneda; compose with the filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful functor to obtain finite presentability. Choose the proved normalized Yoneda-derived Ext comparison. Its additive equivalences, followed by Ext.chgUnivAddEquiv and universe lift, form a natural isomorphism from the large Yoneda functor to the lifted small Ext functor. Transport preservation along it and reflect it through the fully faithful universe lift. Apply fp2_ind_realization with the finite closure and smallness instances from step 2 and ambient Grothendieckness from step 1. Rewrite its hull using step 3 and select the required six conclusions. All indexing categories remain in universe u+1; no extension lift or additional geometric hypothesis is assumed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NY-03d9ef944 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS on an E7 statement correction: the qcqs X becomes a Noetherian X (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), and nothing else in the statement changes. The original qcqs statement is false, and I checked the counterexample against HRS 2305.18131: Lemma 4.1 (line 424), Example 4.2 (line 451), Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 6.12. Take X = Spec C_lc(βN,k), which is w-contractible, qcqs and not Noetherian, with Λ = Q_ℓ and f = ext(ℓ^n). Every term of a finite complex is lisse, so the complex is F(P) for a perfect P. Since R is semi-hereditary, F has amplitude [-1,0], and the two-column sequence makes the counit F_0Γ → id injective on every N_K and on their filtered colimits. For B = im f the counit is Λ_X → B with kernel ker f ≠ 0, nonzero on ∂X. Since Q = coker f lies in I_X, kernel closure fails. This matches the earlier NN 8712600d review, which already called this node refuted. Step 1: the sieve-site theorem at Z, the closed sheaf tensor (which gives additivity) and the modobj theorem make A_X Grothendieck; I accept the three generic tool_uses. Step 2: the noetherian-scalar-constructible-heart node has exactly the item's setting and gives smallness, zero and kernel/cokernel/extension closure. Step 3 (elementary): ker d^0 and im d^{-1} = coker(ker d^{-1} → K^{-1}) lie in C_X, so N_K does too; with C[0] this gives I_X = J. Step 4: the noetherian-scalar-constructible-fp2 node gives the Hom and Yoneda Ext^1 bijections that fp2-ind-realization needs; all its hypotheses are met and its conclusion is the item's (extensions without a lift, coproducts, same universe). The route follows the sk-prop-ind-heart proof; no SGA is used. Edge cases: empty X, zero ring, finite non-regular A (inherits the FP2 WANTED). There are no new nodes and no duplicates. No fixes. Maintainer notes: (1) live reviewed parent lem-sfb-closed-torsion-rigidity-serre-transfer step 2 applies this item to a qcqs T and says 'no Noetherianity'; it must be reopened and the conflict recorded in HUMAN.md, as with O1's torsion-cd-topological-serre-transfer. (2) The title still says qcqs.

statement_change.old_statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Omega\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps, also for $\Omega$. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; in particular it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\mathcal C_X$ be the finite constant scalar-model constructible modules of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For a cochain complex $K^\bullet$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] having only finitely many nonzero terms, all in $\mathcal C_X$, set
$$N_K=H^0(K^\bullet)=\ker(d^0:K^0\to K^1)/\operatorname{im}(d^{-1}:K^{-1}\to K^0).$$
The differentials are arbitrary module-sheaf maps; $N_K$ need not be constructible. Let $\mathcal I_X$ be the replete class of modules isomorphic to small filtered colimits in $\mathcal A_X$ of the modules $N_K$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Diagram arrows may be arbitrary module maps and need not lift to chain maps. Then $\mathcal I_X$ contains zero and $\mathcal C_X$, is closed under kernels and cokernels of all morphisms between its members, under all ambient extensions, and under all small ambient coproducts. Ambient extension closure means that every exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ with $M',M''\in\mathcal I_X$ has $M\in\mathcal I_X$, without a supplied finite-stage lift. All resulting presentations use the same indexing universe. The Noetherian hypothesis is required for this heart argument. No absolute cohomological-dimension bound, affineness, characteristic restriction, invertibility of $\ell$, completeness of the modules, or finite-subextension-valued convention for $\Omega$ is assumed. Empty schemes and zero coefficient rings are included.
